newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates fall on Central Bank cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates fall on Central Bank cut.

text.p: * Banks seen to be more liquid from maturing T-bills
Philippine interbank call loan rates fell to an average of 10.90625 on Tuesday from 11.34375 percent after the Central Bank cut its overnight rates, traders said.
The Central Bank lowered its overnight borrowing rate to 10.75 from 11 percent and its overnight lending rate to 13.25 from 14 percent.
Dealers said the Central Bank's lower rates were in step with the liquid position of banks.

"By the end of this week, it's going to be more liquid," said a foreign bank trader, adding that some 5.1 billion pesos of T-bills are expected to mature on Wednesday. These are in addition to the 4.9 billion pesos of T-notes that matured early this week.
Traders also said banks were swamped with cash since there was no Treasury bill sale held this week due to the holidays for the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
And since Friday, the Central Bank had not been borrowing through reverse repos and special series T-bills.
In the secondary market trading of T-bills, dealers said banks were buying T-bills to service the requirements of clients whose holdings will mature this Wednesday.
The three-month bill had a bid rate of 11.60 to 11.875 percent; the six months at 12.20 to 12.425; and the one year at 12.75 to 12.80.
